item.title: Is Fifa selling parts of the World Cup to private investors?
item.description: This week Fifa announced it will form a new subsidiary company to run part of the World Cup and offer a 20% stake.

item.title: Myanmar court sentences activists to 37 years over election protest
item.description: Nine activists face prison terms of up to 37 years for protesting the military-backed December elections.

item.title: FIFA charges Argentina after World Cup final brawl with Spain
item.description: FIFA hits Argentina with World Cup charges for scuffle after final with Spain and 'Malvinas' banner after England game.

item.title: Trump threatens Iran strikes after attack on US base in Jordan
item.description: ”It’s our turn.” President Donald Trump says the US will hit Iran “very hard” following an attack on US forces in Jordan

item.description: US and Saudi forces launched coordinated airstrikes targeting Iran-backed Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF) bases

item.title: Trump’s attorney general pick faces possible Republican roadblock
item.description: Todd Blanche, Trump's former defence lawyer, has faced scrutiny over his alleged loyalty to the US president.

item.title: Algeria elects first-ever woman speaker of parliament
item.description: Khalida Boufedeche of the National Liberation Front has become the first-ever woman speaker of Algeria’s parliament.

item.title: How is Islamabad handling crisis in Pakistan-administered Kashmir?
item.description: Fatal confrontations between security forces and protesters have marred local elections.

item.title: James Comey’s lawyers say US government distorted details in seashell case
item.description: Case centres on social media post featuring seashells that prosecutors allege is a reference to killing President Trump.

item.title: New investigation shows how an Israeli settler escaped justice
item.description: A Palestinian rights' group found that an Israeli settler killed Awdah Hathaleen but is still escaping justice.

item.title: Ice cream for education: Gaza cafe raises funds for studies
item.description: In war-torn Gaza, a group of Palestinian students opened Flora, an ice cream shop and cafe, to pay university fees.

item.title: Al-Shabab kills five Kenyan security personnel in ambush
item.description: The ambush is part of a rapid surge in cross-border attacks along Kenya's northern frontier.

item.title: Hindus take holy dip in India’s rivers on sacred holiday
item.description: Footage shows tens of thousands of Hindu devotees bathing in India’s Ganga and Saryu rivers to mark Guru Purnima.

item.description: Dr Anthony Fauci declined to answer questions at a Senate hearing on the origins of the Covid-19 pandemic.

item.title: US Fed holds interest rates steady, citing ‘elevated’ inflation
item.description: Elevated inflation partly reflects supply shocks that have increased prices, including of energy, the Fed said.

item.title: Libya electricity blackout protests expose country’s failing grid
item.description: Libyans protest severe power cuts, demanding an end to corruption and grid decay.

item.description: Trump Media has discussed charging as much as $100,000 a month for the Truth API product for buyers to get first access.

item.description: Physician declines to answer Senate questions as Republicans like Rand Paul accuse him of covering up COVID's origins.
